title: Kamat Hotels (India) Ltd - 526668 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Kamat Hotels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 19% YoY to INR 110 crore, with EBITDA margin at 29%, and FY26 revenue INR 386 crore (+8%).
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR 110 crore (+19% YoY), EBITDA of INR 32 crore (29% margin, +213 bps) and PAT of INR 18 crore (+59% YoY, 16% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR 386 crore (+8%), EBITDA INR 97 crore (25.1% margin) and PAT INR 39 crore (10.1% margin). Brand-level ARR and occupancy fell YoY because new hotels are still ramping up, and IRA Mumbai (a leased property, about INR 50 crore revenue) has been vacated from 31 March 2026. Management guided to a cautious outlook, did not give FY27 top-line guidance, and announced Milind Wadekar as incoming CFO.

financial_highlights.change: Management cited ~4% compression FY25 to FY26 when questioned
Includes ~INR 3 crore income tax refund, rent, and INR 5 crore Ilex loan repayment with interest; breakdown promised

segments.name: IRA by Orchid Mumbai (leased)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 50 crore revenue and about INR 20 crore EBITDA; management says EBITDA impact after closure is positive by INR 1-2 crore. Property was vacated after the owner ended the lease from 31 March 2026.

segments.name: Fort Jadhavgadh
segments.commentary: Occupancy and ARR fell sharply YoY (management referenced a 26% dip in the call); management attributed this to leadership change and sales-strategy issues, expects better FY27, and says the property is profitable.

segments.name: IRA by Orchid Porvorim (45 rooms)
segments.commentary: Ramping up after an initial slow period; management says it is now doing exceedingly well through OTA and web channels.

segments.name: Newer properties (Chandigarh, Rishivan, Sambhaji Nagar, Panchgani etc.)
segments.commentary: Management estimated about INR 10 crore EBITDA drag from pre-opening and ramp-up costs, of which about INR 6 crore should be absorbed through operations; about 250-260 keys were added in FY26. Chandigarh delivered INR 14 crore revenue in FY26 against an INR 20-22 crore target.

guidance_outlook: Management is cautiously optimistic and pragmatic on volumes, with focus on domestic demand; no FY27 top-line growth guidance given (explicitly declined to speculate).
Management expects IRA Mumbai exit to reduce FY27 revenue by about INR 50 crore, to be offset by ramp-up of newer hotels and new openings and tie-ups.
Expects to operationalise at least 150-200 keys in FY27 (based on current pipeline).
IRA by Orchid Bhavnagar expected to open by June 2026; Orchid Dehradun estimated for September 2026 (already delayed).
Wage code impact of about INR 4 crore is recurring; about INR 2 crore one-time IRA closure payout (one-month salary, gratuity) is non-recurring.
Labour cost target about 20-23% of revenue for matured hotels.
Management reports no additional payroll burden from absorbing IRA Mumbai staff.
capex_capacity: Upcoming projects delayed: Orchid Dehradun (estimated September 2026), Orchid Gwalior, IRA by Orchid Bhavnagar (June 2026), Orchid Nashik.
New project execution is challenged by LPG-linked shortages of tiles and imported materials; timelines and costs are uncertain.
Expansions are funded from internal accruals, per management.
IRA by Orchid Porvorim is a 45-room hotel that has added to the brand base.
Ilex Developers (IRA Orchid Bhubaneswar): company holds about 32% stake; no current plan to increase, per management.
demand_pricing: Wedding and domestic MICE demand described as very good; majority domestic client base limited exposure to foreign travel disruption.

Brand-level ARR and occupancy fell YoY, which management attributed to the wider base from newly added hotels still ramping up on OTAs; Orchid Mumbai standalone ARR was slightly lower with occupancy up a few percentage points.
Chandigarh was hit last year by airport closure; management expects improved performance this year.
Orchid Passaros child-free positioning is seeing rising advance enquiries, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARR and occupancy fall YoY at IRA and Fort Jadhavgadh, and will EBITDA and PAT be lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand-level metrics fell because of new hotels with a wider base; Jadhavgadh had a mid-year slump, and a strategy change is under way. Management said the current EBITDA already reflects this, with gains expected next year as hotels mature.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IRA Mumbai contribution, and how will it be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IRA Mumbai contributed about INR 50 crore revenue and about INR 20 crore EBITDA, and that the exit is roughly EBITDA-positive by INR 1-2 crore. Replacement will come from maturing hotels, new openings and tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 4% EBITDA compression, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wage code revisions add about INR 4 crore, which is permanent. About INR 2 crore is a one-time IRA closure payout, and newer hotels' payroll costs should be absorbed as they mature.

qa_highlights.question: Why are finance costs around INR 10 crore while borrowings fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not answer on the call and promised a follow-up. Other income of about INR 10 crore includes rent, interest from group companies, a INR 5 crore Ilex loan repayment and about INR 3 crore tax refund; a breakdown was promised.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 top line grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, but acknowledged the INR 50 crore IRA loss would reduce top line unless offset by other properties.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA drag from new properties and how many keys were added?
qa_highlights.answer: About 250-260 keys were added in FY26. The EBITDA drag is about INR 10 crore, of which about INR 6 crore should be absorbed into the gross operating profit (GOP) in the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold INR 40 crore of cash rather than prepay debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers to hold cash as a contingency buffer rather than prepay the INR 86 crore loan at 9.75%, given the risk of shocks.

risks_watch: Top-line base falls by about INR 50 crore after IRA Mumbai exit; FY27 growth depends on ramp-up of new keys.
Fort Jadhavgadh occupancy and ARR recovery after strategy change; the company did not disclose a target occupancy.
Project delays (Dehradun, Gwalior, Nashik) linked to LPG-driven material shortages and owner-led timelines.
Recurring wage code cost increase and labour cost inflation.
Other income of about INR 10 crore and finance cost of about INR 10 crore queried but not fully explained; breakdown promised.
Transition to new CFO Milind Wadekar.
summary.management_tone: Management sounded confident about existing hotels and cautious about new projects and the outlook, and was evasive on FY27 top-line guidance and on finance-cost details. It repeatedly described new-hotel ramp-up as temporary and attributed the margin pressure mainly to wage code and one-time closure costs.
key_quotes: So, looking ahead, we are, like I mentioned, cautiously optimistic.
I would not like to speculate anything right now.
So, the cash which is there, which is generated, is helping us enhance our properties or do the expansion or whatever the things are there.

adds.what: IRA by Orchid Bhavnagar hotel opening
Orchid Dehradun hotel (estimated September 2026, already delayed)
At least 150-200 keys to be operationalised in FY27 from current pipeline

growth.why: No FY27 top-line guidance given; management cited 150-200 new keys to be operationalised in FY27 from the current pipeline and expects ~INR 50 crore revenue loss from the IRA Mumbai exit to be offset by ramp-up of newer hotels, but Dehradun is already delayed to September 2026 and project execution faces material shortages.

mgmt.note: Milind Wadekar announced as incoming CFO; no stated growth plan from him on the call.
